In the absence of Barry Sawyer, Ken Miller, Clive Shippen, Laurie O'Hara, Derek Crookes and George Williams from the A team our hopes of a place as in the 1961 race were reduced to nil and the best we could do was to take 12th position out of the 69 teams that finished.

Pat Newell and Derek Crookes, who have always looked ideally suited to road running, have shown by recent performances that 'life on the road' might well bring them considerable success - providing, of course, they can find time to reel off the extra mileage in training.

Seven Belgravians started in this very large field and Derek Crookes ran particularly well. This is always a high-class field and when runners like Cooke (Portsmouth), O'Sullivan (Oxford ),Franklin (Tipton), Hill-Cottingham (Chelms) and Snowden (Surrey) all finish in the thirties, it is decidedly tough.
John Moore and Derek Crookes were running together a little further back and it was clear we would finish 6 in 40 despite the retirement of John Thresher and Bill Kerr.

From left to right, Norman Stairs, Barry Sawyer, Alan Bishop, Len Bishop, John Moore, Charlie Walker, Denis Jones, and Derek Crookes. This picture was taken at Windsor Castle just before they were sent on their way by Her Majesty The Queen.

How glad we are to see Derek Crookes about again after a serious internal operation, and to know he will be running again next year. Joe Colman is in hospital undergoing a leg operation and we wish him well.
It was good to see Derek Crookes fully recovered from his serious illness and to witness John Hilton's pleasure in clocking his best time to date.

Jack Brown and Mike Shingles also ran well to finish 7th and 10th respectively,but we still only managed 2nd team behind Maidstone who packed 3,4 and 5. Outside the scoring three were the "Duke's Joggers",namely Gordon Biscoe,Joe McDonald,Derek Crookes and Charlie Smart.

The rest of the field led by O'Riordan (Donore H),were nearly half a minute away but it was not long after that John Bicourt crossed the line in 16th place after a very fine run. Gerry and John were our only top men present and Bels had to wait until 88th position for their 3rd scorer to appear (Derek Crookes).
Charlie Walker,who suffered from an attack of stitch,led us home in 43rd place followed closely by Derek Crookes 46th. George Piddington completed our scoring team in 73rd place.
Mike Shingles and Derek Crookes ran well to finish 13th and 16th respectively. John Dear, who started fast, fell back a little but still finished 19th.
When the first Hog's Back race was held in 1958 Belgrave just scraped up a team of the bare scoring three:- Derek Crookes, Jim Radford and Alan Bishop.

Derek Crookes had a recurrence of his stomach trouble recently and had to undergo another operation. We are pleased to say that he is now convalescing, but he is unlikely to do any serious running again.
Derek Crookes writes to say that he has heard from PAT & ALAN MEAD who are now happily settled in Australia. Alan has given up serious training and turned to surfing---who can blame him?
